drug_class: Orexin receptor antagonist (dual orexin receptor antagonist / DORA)
purpose: Daridorexant is used to help adults who have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep (insomnia). It helps you get to sleep faster and stay asleep longer so you feel more rested. It is meant for ongoing use, not just a single night.
how_it_works: Your brain makes chemicals called orexins that keep you awake and alert. Daridorexant works by blocking those 'wake-up' signals in your brain, allowing your body to naturally drift into sleep. Unlike older sleep medicines, it targets only the wake system rather than slowing down your whole brain.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, dizziness, drowsiness or feeling sleepy the next morning, nausea, and feeling tired. Most people tolerate it well, but let your doctor or pharmacist know if any side effect bothers you.
warnings: Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that needs full alertness the morning after taking this medicine, as you may still feel drowsy. Avoid alcohol while taking daridorexant as it can increase drowsiness. It can rarely cause sleep-related behaviors like sleepwalking or sleep-driving — stop it and call your doctor if this happens. It may worsen depression or cause unusual thoughts; tell your doctor if you have a history of mental health issues. It is a controlled substance (Schedule IV), so only take it exactly as prescribed and do not share it with others.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 25 mg taken by mouth once per night, right before going to bed, with at least 7 hours remaining before you need to wake up. Your doctor may increase your dose to 50 mg if needed. Do not take it with or right after a heavy or high-fat meal, as this can slow how quickly it works.
